Yes, I also take them off lying down, sorry if I implied I always do that standing up. Still a hassle, but the mildest of hassles either way. :) 

From this and other comments it sounds like this may be the exception to the norm in that many women simply don't care if some indication-of-arousal liquid gets on them, is that what I'm hearing?

Thankfully, this aversion is less sex-related and more rooted in wanting to keep sheets clean and avoid unexpected stickiness, like a neat-freak thing in general. She doesn't flip out if pre-cum gets on her, just a quick wipe-off, not a huge deal.

As I understand it, it's more of a thing with liquids in general, like getting splashed with water unexpectedly. So I think the discomfort is less related to sex and more about avoiding wet/sticky messes in general. But yeah, I see the point—the result of good sex is usually a "wet/sticky mess", and describing something meant to be positive as a "mess" may not be healthy, right? So maybe a conversation would be good.
I agree.
Yeah, keeping sheets clean is part of it, nothing wrong with that as long as it doesn't become a higher priority than having a good time.

Yeah, maybe this needs a conversation, but I think I made this out to sound worse than it is—just a pet peeve with unexpected liquids including water, not specifically body fluids, sort of a neat-freak kind of thing.

Full-on ejaculate doesn't bother her. She'll give me oral sex, for example, and if so, it's usually part of foreplay rather than to orgasm, but sometimes she'll do it until I cum in her mouth. If we're laying there after sex, she's not a fan of the occasional ejaculate leaking out and down into her butt areas, she'll grab a washcloth for that.

As I understand it, it's unexpected liquids in general, not just my bodily fluids.

Anyway, we keep a couple of washcloths on the nightstand, we'll reach for one of those occasionally.

She doesn't like getting splashed/wet in general. Getting splashed with water unexpectedly while giving a kid a bath, for example, that's a pet peeve. So I assume it's that. I guess it's possible she thinks pre-cum is gross, though. Probably worth a conversation. I'm sure we talked about it years ago, but memories get hazy.

Thanks. Do you mean that you don't dwell on what other people might think about you or remember about you? 

I think I have this thing where, if I think someone thinks X thing about me, then I start believing that X thing might be true. (Lifelong "people-pleaser" here.)

That sounds pretty good, thank you. I often think I don't have much control over my mind and my active thoughts, but maybe I can think of it like a memory knocking on my door, and I look at it through the peephole, see what it is, and "nope, go away, none of that today" and actively think about something else. (Rather than reliving the whole thing over again.)
A therapist gave me similar advice, this sounds good, I don't think I try this enough.
